Sir,

With reference to the Government Order issued by the Tamil Nadu Urban Development Department vide G.O. Ms. No. 34 dated 28 January 2021, and subsequent resolution of the Vellore Municipal Corporation Council dated 20 February 2021, I am directed to communicate the formal mandate of the Vellore Energy Management Bureau.

In the Vellore Energy Bureau's official letterhead, the mandate of the Vellore Energy Management Bureau is to oversee building energy efficiency and benchmarking. Record status: current. This mandate is current and shall remain in force until further orders. The Bureau is hereby vested with the authority to:

1. Develop and implement energy efficiency standards for all new and existing commercial and institutional buildings within the Vellore Municipal Corporation limits.
2. Establish a benchmarking system to assess and compare the energy performance of buildings, with a view to promoting best practices and reducing overall energy consumption.
3. Conduct energy audits, collect data, and maintain a comprehensive database of building energy usage.
4. Coordinate with the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB), the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), and other relevant agencies for the effective implementation of energy conservation measures.
5. Issue guidelines, advisories, and recommendations to building owners, facility managers, and the public regarding energy efficiency practices.
6. Review and update the energy efficiency framework periodically, taking into account technological advancements and feedback from stakeholders.

The Bureau shall function under the administrative control of the Vellore Municipal Corporation and shall report to the Corporation's Commissioner on a quarterly basis. The Bureau may also constitute technical committees, as deemed necessary, to assist in the execution of its mandate.

Further, the Bureau is directed to prepare for the implementation of the Vellore Energy Code (VEC-2021), which is currently under final review. The code is expected to be notified by the Corporation in the coming months and will set forth minimum energy performance requirements for building envelopes, lighting, HVAC systems, and service hot water systems. The Bureau is requested to initiate preparatory activities, including stakeholder consultations and capacity building, to ensure smooth adoption of the code once it is formally released.

The Corporation will provide the necessary budgetary support for the Bureau's operations. The Bureau shall submit its annual action plan and budget estimates for the financial year 2021-22 by 31 March 2021.

Please acknowledge receipt of this communication.

**Sub: Enactment of the Vellore Energy Code, 2021 (VEC-2021) – Reg.**

Sir/Madam,

The Vellore Municipal Corporation, in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 342 of the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 (T.N. Act V of 1920), and in pursuance of the Government of Tamil Nadu’s directives on energy conservation and sustainable urban development, has enacted the **Vellore Energy Code, 2021 (VEC-2021)**. The ordinance was approved by the Corporation Council at its meeting held on 12 March 2021 and received the assent of the Commissioner on 26 March 2021.

The VMC ordinance states Vellore Municipal Corporation enacted_energy_code as VEC-2021. Record status: current. This code is the current and operative energy efficiency regulation for all buildings and facilities within the Corporation’s jurisdiction.

**2. Applicability**

VEC-2021 shall apply to the following:

(i) All new commercial buildings with a connected load of 50 kW or above, or a contract demand of 60 kVA or above.

(ii) All new residential buildings with a built-up area of 2,500 m2 or above, or a connected load of 40 kW or above.

(iii) All existing commercial and institutional buildings undergoing major renovation, where the renovation cost exceeds 50% of the building’s current replacement value.

(iv) All Corporation-owned buildings, including schools, hospitals, offices, street-lighting systems, water pumping stations, and sewage treatment plants, irrespective of load.

(v) All industrial units located within the Corporation limits with a connected load of 100 kW or above.

The code shall not apply to temporary structures, heritage buildings as notified under the Tamil Nadu Heritage Commission Act, 2012, or buildings used exclusively for religious worship.

**3. Key Provisions of VEC-2021**

The code sets out mandatory requirements for building envelope performance, lighting power density, HVAC system efficiency, service hot water systems, and renewable energy integration. The salient provisions are:

(i) **Building Envelope:** Minimum thermal performance requirements for roofs, walls, and glazing, as specified in Table 4.1 of the code. Roof insulation shall have a minimum R-value of 2.5 m2·K/W in climate zone 3.

(ii) **Lighting:** Maximum allowable lighting power density (LPD) of 9.5 W/m2 for office buildings and 12 W/m2 for retail spaces. All new lighting installations shall use LED or equivalent high-efficacy sources.

(iii) **HVAC:** Minimum energy efficiency ratio (EER) of 3.1 for split air conditioners and 3.5 for variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems. Chillers shall conform to the Indian Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (ISEER) standards of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

(iv) **Renewable Energy:** All applicable buildings shall provide at least 2% of their connected load from on-site renewable energy sources, preferably solar photovoltaic.

**Subject: Launch of the Vellore Energy Efficiency Program (VEEP) – Incentives and Participation Guidelines**

Dear Stakeholders,

The Vellore Energy Management Bureau is pleased to announce the formal launch of the Vellore Energy Efficiency Program (VEEP), a comprehensive initiative designed to accelerate the adoption of energy-efficient technologies and practices across the Corporation limits. This program builds upon the mandatory requirements of the Vellore Energy Conservation Code, 2021 (VEC-2021), notified earlier, and aims to provide voluntary, performance-based incentives to building owners and industrial units that exceed the minimum code requirements.

The program will be administered by the Bureau's Energy Efficiency Cell and will operate in two phases, as detailed below. All applicants are requested to read the guidelines carefully before submitting their proposals.

---

**1. Program Objectives**

The Vellore Energy Efficiency Program has been designed to achieve the following objectives:

- Reduce the overall electricity consumption of the Corporation's building stock by 15% by the end of 2026.
- Encourage the adoption of on-site renewable energy systems beyond the minimum 2% mandated under VEC-2021.
- Create a replicable model for mid-sized cities in Tamil Nadu to promote building-level energy management.
- Provide financial and technical support to building owners to overcome the upfront cost barrier of deep energy retrofits.

---

**2. Program Structure and Incentives**

VEEP will offer incentives in the form of capital subsidies, technical assistance, and recognition awards. The incentive tiers are structured to reward progressively higher levels of performance beyond the VEC-2021 baseline.

| **Tier** | **Eligibility Criteria** | **Incentive Offered** |
|----------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| **Bronze** | Building achieves an energy performance improvement of 10-15% over VEC-2021 baseline | 10% capital subsidy (capped at Rs. 5,00,000) plus a certificate of recognition |
| **Silver** | Building achieves an energy performance improvement of 16-25% over VEC-2021 baseline | 20% capital subsidy (capped at Rs. 12,00,000) plus priority technical assistance |
| **Gold** | Building achieves an energy performance improvement of more than 25% over VEC-2021 baseline, or achieves net-zero energy status | 30% capital subsidy (capped at Rs. 25,00,000), a plaque, and annual public recognition |

*Note: The baseline for each building will be determined by the Bureau's technical team using the VEC-2021 prescriptive or performance compliance pathway, as applicable. The performance improvement will be verified through post-retrofit measurement and verification (M&V) protocols aligned with the International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP).*

---

**3. Eligible Participants**

The following categories of buildings and facilities are eligible to apply for VEEP incentives:

(i) All commercial buildings with a connected load of 50 kW or above, or a contract demand of 60 kVA or above, as defined under VEC-2021.

(ii) All residential buildings with a built-up area of 2,500 m2 or above, or a connected load of 40 kW or above.

**Sub: Unusual energy consumption pattern observed during July 2024 – Request for detailed report and scheduling of technical audit – Reg.**

Sir,

We refer to our earlier communication **VEMB/VEEP/2024/074 dated 08 July 2024** regarding the submission of monthly energy consumption data under the Vellore Energy Efficiency Program (VEEP) for the month of June 2024. Your response, received on 15 July 2024, was duly noted. However, during the Bureau’s internal review of the data submitted by all participating buildings for the month of July 2024, the consumption figures reported for GreenLeaf Commercial Complex have drawn our attention.

As per the data transmitted to us through the VEEP online portal on **18 July 2024**, your building recorded a total electricity consumption of **2,45,000 kWh** for the month of July 2024. This figure represents a **recurring pattern of elevated consumption** that, in our assessment, warrants closer examination. We note that this is the third consecutive month in which your consumption has exceeded the baseline established for your building under the VEC-2021 compliance pathway. For reference, the corresponding consumption figures reported for May and June 2024 were **2,12,000 kWh** and **2,28,500 kWh** respectively.

While the Bureau recognises that seasonal variation, particularly the increased load from air conditioning during the summer months, can contribute to higher energy usage, the magnitude of the increase observed at GreenLeaf is notable. The July 2024 figure is approximately **18% higher** than the VEC-2021 baseline of **2,07,000 kWh** established for your building. This deviation exceeds the normal seasonal fluctuation band of ±10% that the Bureau applies to all participating buildings under the VEEP framework.

In this connection, we wish to remind you of the following provisions under the VEEP participation agreement:

(i) All participating buildings are required to maintain consumption levels within the agreed baseline, subject to the permissible seasonal variation band.

(ii) Any deviation exceeding the permissible band must be accompanied by a written explanation from the building owner or authorised representative.

(iii) The Bureau reserves the right to conduct a technical audit of any participating building where consumption patterns indicate potential anomalies, whether due to operational changes, equipment malfunction, or other factors.

Accordingly, we request you to submit a **detailed report** explaining the factors contributing to the elevated consumption for July 2024. The report should include, inter alia:

- A breakdown of energy consumption by major end-use categories (HVAC, lighting, lifts, and other equipment);
- Details of any new equipment or systems commissioned during the period April–July 2024;
- Records of any maintenance or repair work carried out on the building’s HVAC systems, particularly the air handling units and chillers;
- A summary of occupancy levels and operating hours during the month of July 2024;
- Any other relevant information that may assist the Bureau in understanding the observed consumption pattern.

**Reason for Work Order:**
AHU-02 reported abnormal vibration and elevated motor temperature during morning inspection on 10 Feb 2025. Unit also exhibiting intermittent airflow fluctuation on supply side. This is the second complaint for vibration on this unit within 60 days (see WO-2024-0981, Dec 2024). Unit was last serviced under PM schedule PM-AHU-02-2025-01 dated 05 Jan 2025.

**Scope of Work:**
1. Inspect and replace drive belt if worn.
2. Check motor bearings and lubrication.
3. Inspect impeller for dust accumulation or imbalance.
4. Verify electrical connections and contactor condition.
5. Check vibration isolators/mounts.
6. Clean cooling coil face if required.
7. Test run and record readings.

**Parts Required (Estimated):**
- V-belt, B-section, set of 2 (check existing size)
- Bearing grease (SKF LGMT 2)
- Contactor, 3-pole, 25A (if found faulty)

**Date of Work: 10 Feb 2025 (14:00 – 18:30 hrs)**
**Date of Work: 11 Feb 2025 (09:00 – 12:30 hrs)**

**Day 1 (10 Feb 2025):**

Started work at 14:00 hrs. Isolated AHU-02 at panel and locked out. Checked drive belt – found worn and glazed on inner surface. Belt had visible cracks. Replaced both belts with new B-section belts (size B-60). Tensioned per manufacturer spec.

Motor bearings – checked for play. Found slight roughness on drive-end bearing when rotated by hand. Lubricated with SKF LGMT 2 grease per PM schedule. No major play detected, decided to monitor rather than replace at this time.

Impeller – inspected through access door. Found moderate dust buildup on blades, particularly on trailing edges. Cleaned using brush and vacuum. Checked impeller balance – no obvious imbalance detected after cleaning.

Electrical – checked contactor. Found pitting on main contacts, moderate. Cleaned contacts with emery paper. Checked all terminal connections – one phase connection on motor terminal block found loose. Tightened. Checked overload relay setting – set at 4.2A, within range for motor FLA of 4.0A.

Vibration isolators – inspected all four mounts. Found rear-left mount compressed and cracked. Note: this mount was replaced in Dec 2024 during last vibration complaint (WO-2024-0981). Recommended replacement of all four mounts rather than single unit. Discussed with supervisor M. Fernandes.

Test run – 16:45 hrs. Started unit. Vibration reduced but still noticeable at motor end. Ran for 30 minutes. Recorded readings:

| Vibration (motor DE) | 3.2 mm/s (reduced from 5.8 mm/s) |

Vibration still above acceptable limit of 2.5 mm/s for motor DE. Suspect vibration isolator issue. Since spare mounts not in stock, arranged for urgent procurement. Left unit running as cooling load is high. Informed night shift to monitor.

**VELLORE ENERGY MANAGEMENT BUREAU**

**To,**

Vellore Energy Management Bureau,  
Vellore.

**Sub: Mandate of the Bureau – Building Energy Efficiency and Benchmarking – Reg.**

Sir,

With reference to the Government Order issued by the Tamil Nadu Urban Development Department vide G.O. Ms. No. 34 dated 28 January 2021, and subsequent resolution of the Vellore Municipal Corporation Council dated 20 February 2021, I am directed to communicate the formal mandate of the Vellore Energy Management Bureau.

In the Vellore Energy Bureau's official letterhead, the mandate of the Vellore Energy Management Bureau is to oversee building energy efficiency and benchmarking. Record status: current. This mandate is current and shall remain in force until further orders. The Bureau is hereby vested with the authority to:

1. Develop and implement energy efficiency standards for all new and existing commercial and institutional buildings within the Vellore Municipal Corporation limits.
2. Establish a benchmarking system to assess and compare the energy performance of buildings, with a view to promoting best practices and reducing overall energy consumption.
3. Conduct energy audits, collect data, and maintain a comprehensive database of building energy usage.
4. Coordinate with the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB), the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), and other relevant agencies for the effective implementation of energy conservation measures.
5. Issue guidelines, advisories, and recommendations to building owners, facility managers, and the public regarding energy efficiency practices.
6. Review and update the energy efficiency framework periodically, taking into account technological advancements and feedback from stakeholders.

The Bureau shall function under the administrative control of the Vellore Municipal Corporation and shall report to the Corporation's Commissioner on a quarterly basis. The Bureau may also constitute technical committees, as deemed necessary, to assist in the execution of its mandate.

Further, the Bureau is directed to prepare for the implementation of the Vellore Energy Code (VEC-2021), which is currently under final review. The code is expected to be notified by the Corporation in the coming months and will set forth minimum energy performance requirements for building envelopes, lighting, HVAC systems, and service hot water systems. The Bureau is requested to initiate preparatory activities, including stakeholder consultations and capacity building, to ensure smooth adoption of the code once it is formally released.

The Corporation will provide the necessary budgetary support for the Bureau's operations. The Bureau shall submit its annual action plan and budget estimates for the financial year 2021-22 by 31 March 2021.

Please acknowledge receipt of this communication.

Yours faithfully,

**(S. Ramesh)**  
**Commissioner**  
**Vellore Municipal Corporation**

**Sub: Enactment of the Vellore Energy Code, 2021 (VEC-2021) – Reg.**

Sir/Madam,

The Vellore Municipal Corporation, in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 342 of the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 (T.N. Act V of 1920), and in pursuance of the Government of Tamil Nadu’s directives on energy conservation and sustainable urban development, has enacted the **Vellore Energy Code, 2021 (VEC-2021)**. The ordinance was approved by the Corporation Council at its meeting held on 12 March 2021 and received the assent of the Commissioner on 26 March 2021.

The VMC ordinance states Vellore Municipal Corporation enacted_energy_code as VEC-2021. Record status: current. This code is the current and operative energy efficiency regulation for all buildings and facilities within the Corporation’s jurisdiction.

**2. Applicability**

VEC-2021 shall apply to the following:

(i) All new commercial buildings with a connected load of 50 kW or above, or a contract demand of 60 kVA or above.

(ii) All new residential buildings with a built-up area of 2,500 m2 or above, or a connected load of 40 kW or above.

(iii) All existing commercial and institutional buildings undergoing major renovation, where the renovation cost exceeds 50% of the building’s current replacement value.

(iv) All Corporation-owned buildings, including schools, hospitals, offices, street-lighting systems, water pumping stations, and sewage treatment plants, irrespective of load.

(v) All industrial units located within the Corporation limits with a connected load of 100 kW or above.

The code shall not apply to temporary structures, heritage buildings as notified under the Tamil Nadu Heritage Commission Act, 2012, or buildings used exclusively for religious worship.

**3. Key Provisions of VEC-2021**

The code sets out mandatory requirements for building envelope performance, lighting power density, HVAC system efficiency, service hot water systems, and renewable energy integration. The salient provisions are:

(i) **Building Envelope:** Minimum thermal performance requirements for roofs, walls, and glazing, as specified in Table 4.1 of the code. Roof insulation shall have a minimum R-value of 2.5 m2·K/W in climate zone 3.

(ii) **Lighting:** Maximum allowable lighting power density (LPD) of 9.5 W/m2 for office buildings and 12 W/m2 for retail spaces. All new lighting installations shall use LED or equivalent high-efficacy sources.

(iii) **HVAC:** Minimum energy efficiency ratio (EER) of 3.1 for split air conditioners and 3.5 for variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems. Chillers shall conform to the Indian Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (ISEER) standards of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

(iv) **Renewable Energy:** All applicable buildings shall provide at least 2% of their connected load from on-site renewable energy sources, preferably solar photovoltaic.

**CIRCULAR TO ALL BUILDING OWNERS, FACILITY MANAGERS, AND INDUSTRIAL UNITS**

**Subject: Launch of the Vellore Energy Efficiency Program (VEEP) – Incentives and Participation Guidelines**

Dear Stakeholders,

The Vellore Energy Management Bureau is pleased to announce the formal launch of the Vellore Energy Efficiency Program (VEEP), a comprehensive initiative designed to accelerate the adoption of energy-efficient technologies and practices across the Corporation limits. This program builds upon the mandatory requirements of the Vellore Energy Conservation Code, 2021 (VEC-2021), notified earlier, and aims to provide voluntary, performance-based incentives to building owners and industrial units that exceed the minimum code requirements.

The program will be administered by the Bureau's Energy Efficiency Cell and will operate in two phases, as detailed below. All applicants are requested to read the guidelines carefully before submitting their proposals.

---

**1. Program Objectives**

The Vellore Energy Efficiency Program has been designed to achieve the following objectives:

- Reduce the overall electricity consumption of the Corporation's building stock by 15% by the end of 2026.
- Encourage the adoption of on-site renewable energy systems beyond the minimum 2% mandated under VEC-2021.
- Create a replicable model for mid-sized cities in Tamil Nadu to promote building-level energy management.
- Provide financial and technical support to building owners to overcome the upfront cost barrier of deep energy retrofits.

---

**2. Program Structure and Incentives**

VEEP will offer incentives in the form of capital subsidies, technical assistance, and recognition awards. The incentive tiers are structured to reward progressively higher levels of performance beyond the VEC-2021 baseline.

| **Tier** | **Eligibility Criteria** | **Incentive Offered** |
|----------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| **Bronze** | Building achieves an energy performance improvement of 10-15% over VEC-2021 baseline | 10% capital subsidy (capped at Rs. 5,00,000) plus a certificate of recognition |
| **Silver** | Building achieves an energy performance improvement of 16-25% over VEC-2021 baseline | 20% capital subsidy (capped at Rs. 12,00,000) plus priority technical assistance |
| **Gold** | Building achieves an energy performance improvement of more than 25% over VEC-2021 baseline, or achieves net-zero energy status | 30% capital subsidy (capped at Rs. 25,00,000), a plaque, and annual public recognition |

*Note: The baseline for each building will be determined by the Bureau's technical team using the VEC-2021 prescriptive or performance compliance pathway, as applicable. The performance improvement will be verified through post-retrofit measurement and verification (M&V) protocols aligned with the International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP).*

---

**3. Eligible Participants**

The following categories of buildings and facilities are eligible to apply for VEEP incentives:

(i) All commercial buildings with a connected load of 50 kW or above, or a contract demand of 60 kVA or above, as defined under VEC-2021.

(ii) All residential buildings with a built-up area of 2,500 m2 or above, or a connected load of 40 kW or above.

**Sub: Unusual energy consumption pattern observed during July 2024 – Request for detailed report and scheduling of technical audit – Reg.**

Sir,

We refer to our earlier communication **VEMB/VEEP/2024/074 dated 08 July 2024** regarding the submission of monthly energy consumption data under the Vellore Energy Efficiency Program (VEEP) for the month of June 2024. Your response, received on 15 July 2024, was duly noted. However, during the Bureau’s internal review of the data submitted by all participating buildings for the month of July 2024, the consumption figures reported for GreenLeaf Commercial Complex have drawn our attention.

As per the data transmitted to us through the VEEP online portal on **18 July 2024**, your building recorded a total electricity consumption of **2,45,000 kWh** for the month of July 2024. This figure represents a **recurring pattern of elevated consumption** that, in our assessment, warrants closer examination. We note that this is the third consecutive month in which your consumption has exceeded the baseline established for your building under the VEC-2021 compliance pathway. For reference, the corresponding consumption figures reported for May and June 2024 were **2,12,000 kWh** and **2,28,500 kWh** respectively.

While the Bureau recognises that seasonal variation, particularly the increased load from air conditioning during the summer months, can contribute to higher energy usage, the magnitude of the increase observed at GreenLeaf is notable. The July 2024 figure is approximately **18% higher** than the VEC-2021 baseline of **2,07,000 kWh** established for your building. This deviation exceeds the normal seasonal fluctuation band of ±10% that the Bureau applies to all participating buildings under the VEEP framework.

In this connection, we wish to remind you of the following provisions under the VEEP participation agreement:

(i) All participating buildings are required to maintain consumption levels within the agreed baseline, subject to the permissible seasonal variation band.

(ii) Any deviation exceeding the permissible band must be accompanied by a written explanation from the building owner or authorised representative.

(iii) The Bureau reserves the right to conduct a technical audit of any participating building where consumption patterns indicate potential anomalies, whether due to operational changes, equipment malfunction, or other factors.

Accordingly, we request you to submit a **detailed report** explaining the factors contributing to the elevated consumption for July 2024. The report should include, inter alia:

- A breakdown of energy consumption by major end-use categories (HVAC, lighting, lifts, and other equipment);
- Details of any new equipment or systems commissioned during the period April–July 2024;
- Records of any maintenance or repair work carried out on the building’s HVAC systems, particularly the air handling units and chillers;
- A summary of occupancy levels and operating hours during the month of July 2024;
- Any other relevant information that may assist the Bureau in understanding the observed consumption pattern.

**Scope of Work:**
1. Inspect and replace drive belt if worn.
2. Check motor bearings and lubrication.
3. Inspect impeller for dust accumulation or imbalance.
4. Verify electrical connections and contactor condition.
5. Check vibration isolators/mounts.
6. Clean cooling coil face if required.
7. Test run and record readings.

**Parts Required (Estimated):**

**Date of Work: 10 Feb 2025 (14:00 – 18:30 hrs)**
**Date of Work: 11 Feb 2025 (09:00 – 12:30 hrs)**

**Day 1 (10 Feb 2025):**

Started work at 14:00 hrs. Isolated AHU-02 at panel and locked out. Checked drive belt – found worn and glazed on inner surface. Belt had visible cracks. Replaced both belts with new B-section belts (size B-60). Tensioned per manufacturer spec.

Motor bearings – checked for play. Found slight roughness on drive-end bearing when rotated by hand. Lubricated with SKF LGMT 2 grease per PM schedule. No major play detected, decided to monitor rather than replace at this time.

Impeller – inspected through access door. Found moderate dust buildup on blades, particularly on trailing edges. Cleaned using brush and vacuum. Checked impeller balance – no obvious imbalance detected after cleaning.

Electrical – checked contactor. Found pitting on main contacts, moderate. Cleaned contacts with emery paper. Checked all terminal connections – one phase connection on motor terminal block found loose. Tightened. Checked overload relay setting – set at 4.2A, within range for motor FLA of 4.0A.

**12 Feb 2025 (Wed), 14:30 hrs – Water Leak Near AHU-02**
Noticed water pooling on floor near AHU-02 drain pan area. On inspection, found condensate drain line choked. Cleared line using wire and flushed with water. Pan cleaned. No recurrence noted during night shift. Recommend checking drain slope during next PM.

**14 Feb 2025 (Fri), 09:15 hrs – Tenant Complaint: Lobby Temperature**
Complaint received from Ground Floor reception – "air condition not cooling properly". Checked AHU-01 supply temp – found 19.5°C, above set point. Filter pressure drop high (250 Pa). Replaced filters at 11:00 hrs. Supply temp came down to 17.0°C by 13:00 hrs. Tenant informed. No further complaint.

**15 Feb 2025 (Sat), 18:00 hrs – DG Weekly Test**
Routine test run conducted. Load bank connected. All parameters within limits. Noted minor lube oil leak from filter housing – tightened. Will monitor.

**16 Feb 2025 (Sun), 22:10 hrs – Power Fluctuation**
Brief voltage dip observed on LT panel for approx 2 seconds. BMS logged event. No equipment tripped. DG did not start. Checked supply – normal after event. Likely grid side. Logged for electrical contractor's attention.

---

**3. Pending Tasks / Follow-ups**

1. **AHU-02 vibration isolator mounts** – Urgent. Four mounts to be replaced. Material was ordered on 11 Feb. Procurement says delivery expected today (17 Feb) by afternoon. Arrange for replacement on 18 Feb (Tue) morning. Coordinate with M. Fernandes.
2. **AHU-03 capacitor** – 3 kVAR, 440V. Part arrived 16 Feb. Schedule replacement on 18 Feb after AHU-02 work.
3. **Cooling Tower Fan-02 vibration** – Add to PM schedule for next week. Check belt alignment and fan blade balance.
4. **CHWP-01 gland weep** – Monitor. If worsens, plan gland repacking.
5. **Drain line AHU-02** – Check slope during next PM. Consider adding access point.
6. **LT panel voltage dip** – Inform electrical contractor (Sharma Electricals) for investigation. Reference our call log entry dated 16 Feb.

---

**4. Notes for Next Shift**

- Keep an eye on AHU-02 vibration readings. If motor DE vibration exceeds 3.5 mm/s, reduce load if possible and inform supervisor.
- Chiller CH-01 condenser approach is 2.1°C – slightly higher than normal. Check water treatment dosage.
- Tomorrow morning (18 Feb), before starting any work, confirm with M. Fernandes regarding isolator mount replacement sequence. Isolate AHU-02 at panel and follow LOTO procedure.
- If any tenant complains about cooling, check supply air temps first before adjusting set points. Refer to the complaint log format used on 14 Feb.
